document_check.note: Document is Yan J, Li X, Guo X, et al. 'Effect of Multicomponent Exercise on Cognition, Physical Function and Activities of Daily Life in Older Adults With Dementia or Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis', Arch Phys Med Rehabil 2023;104:2092-108. This matches 'Yan et al. 2023, P-603'. The cited g = 0.978 is the pooled effect on global cognition in MCI (p1, p13).

cited_result: Pooled Hedges' g = 0.978 (95% CI 0.298 to 1.659) for the effect of multicomponent exercise on global cognition in MCI, from 10 RCTs with 384 participants, I2 = 93% (p13).
tool_reason: The cited result is a pooled estimate from a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs, so ROBIS applies.

domains.rationale: The protocol was registered, but the intervention criterion contradicts itself: it defines multicomponent exercise as four components, then admits two components plus non-exercise co-interventions, while the review claims to isolate exercise alone. Inclusion is also restricted to English-language publications.

signalling.question: 1.1 Did the review adhere to pre-defined objectives and eligibility criteria?
signalling.quote: and was prospectively registered at the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO Registration No. CRD42022324641)

signalling.question: 1.2 Were the eligibility criteria appropriate for the review question?
signalling.quote: (a) study design: randomized controlled trials (RCTs); (b) participants: mean age ≥60 years old.

signalling.question: 1.3 Were eligibility criteria unambiguous?
signalling.quote: We included studies that included an exercise program consisting of at least 2 of these sports components as well as other nonexercise interventions such as behavioral therapy, cognitive therapy, and electrical and magnetic stimulation. [versus p14:] we isolated the effects of exercise itself, without other concomitant interventions

signalling.question: 1.4 Were all restrictions in eligibility criteria based on study characteristics appropriate?
signalling.quote: There were no limitations on the intensity, frequency, and duration of exercises

signalling.question: 1.5 Were any restrictions in eligibility criteria based on sources of information appropriate?
signalling.quote: The systematic review included studies published in English

domains.rationale: Four major databases were searched and screening was done in duplicate. However, no supplementary search methods are reported, the intervention terms reported are narrow ('circuit-based', 'multicomponent', 'multimodal'), and English-only and conference-abstract restrictions were applied.

signalling.question: 2.1 Did the search include an appropriate range of databases/electronic sources for published and unpublished reports?
signalling.quote: The following electronic databases were searched for relevant English language literature through May 2022: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science

signalling.question: 2.2 Were methods additional to database searching used to identify relevant reports?
signalling.quote: Searched Methods and Results for reference-list checking, citation searching, trial registries, grey literature or contact with experts; none reported.

signalling.question: 2.3 Were the terms and structure of the search strategy likely to retrieve as many eligible studies as possible?
signalling.quote: The search strategy included terms related to circuit-based exercise, multicomponent physical activity, multimodal training, AD, MCI, dementia, and cognitive dysfunction. The terms were combined using the Boolean operators “AND,” “OR,” and “NOT”

signalling.question: 2.4 Were restrictions based on date, publication format, or language appropriate?
signalling.quote: relevant English language literature through May 2022 ... conference abstracts (n=275)

signalling.question: 2.5 Were efforts made to minimise error in selection of studies?
signalling.quote: Two reviewers independently read the title and abstract in accordance with the inclusion criteria

domains.rationale: Extraction was done in duplicate with a third adjudicator, study characteristics were tabulated, missing data were requested from authors, and the Cochrane RoB tool was applied by two independent reviewers.

signalling.question: 3.1 Were efforts made to minimise error in data collection?
signalling.quote: To ensure the accuracy of data entry, data were extracted and checked by 2 reviewers, and any discrepancies were discussed or adjudicated by a third reviewer.

signalling.question: 3.2 Were sufficient study characteristics available for both review authors and readers to be able to interpret the results?
signalling.quote: The following data were extracted: author; year of publication; country where the study was conducted

signalling.question: 3.3 Were all relevant study results collected for use in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: Missing data were obtained where possible by contacting the original authors by e-mail if necessary. Data from the final assessment were included when the study reported outcomes at multiple time points.

signalling.question: 3.4 Was risk of bias (or methodological quality) formally assessed using appropriate criteria?
signalling.quote: Quality assessments of the included literature were conducted by 2 independent reviewers using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool.

signalling.question: 3.5 Were efforts made to minimise error in risk of bias assessment?
signalling.quote: Disagreements were resolved through discussion until consensus was reached on each rating.

domains.rationale: The MCI global cognition pool combines MMSE, ADAS-Cog and MoCA with I2 = 93%, and heterogeneity was not explored beyond random effects and leave-one-out. Three MCI studies in Table 1 report identical baseline data, which suggests the same sample was counted more than once, while the review recognises only one shared-protocol pair. Primary-study risk of bias (all high for blinding) is not incorporated into the synthesis. The headline MCI executive-function estimate follows a post hoc exclusion.

signalling.question: 4.1 Did the synthesis include all studies that it should?
signalling.quote: 3 studies were excluded from quantitative analysis owing to noncomparable or insufficient data

signalling.question: 4.2 Were all pre-defined analyses reported or departures explained?
signalling.quote: When it was removed, after running the meta-analysis again, the benefit of ME on EF remained discernible (g=0.448; 95% CI, 0.171-0.726; P<.05; figure 4B)

signalling.question: 4.3 Was the synthesis appropriate given the nature and similarity in the research questions, study designs and outcomes across included studies?
signalling.quote: aggregating data from 10 trials with 384 participants that used the MMSE or Alzheimer’s Disease Assessment Scale [p11]; Table 1: 'Doi et al,48 Japan RCT MCI N=50 (23, 46.0) MTG: n=25 (12, 48.0) CG: n=25 (11, 44.0)', 'Makizako et al,49 Japan RCT MCI N=50 (23, 46) MTG: n=25 (12, 48) CG: n=25 (11, 44)', 'Suzuki et al,51 Japan RCT MCI N=50 (23, 46)' [p5]; only one pair acknowledged: 'with different outcomes of interest used the same intervention protocol and were performed by the same research team' [p3]

signalling.question: 4.4 Was between-study variation (heterogeneity) minimal or addressed in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: There was no publication bias (Egger test P=.303), but considerable heterogeneity was found (Q=8; I2=93%).

signalling.question: 4.5 Were the findings robust, e.g. as demonstrated through funnel plot or sensitivity analyses?
signalling.quote: The sensitivity analysis did not overturn the conclusion we drew from 10 trials

signalling.question: 4.6 Were biases in primary studies minimal or addressed in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: Participants and researchers could not be blinded because of the nature of the intervention. Consequently, the bias of all studies was deemed high risk.

domains.domain: Phase 3. Risk of bias in the review
domains.rationale: The authors acknowledge heterogeneity, small studies and publication bias. However, they conclude that the findings 'confirm the viability' of the intervention without addressing the uniformly high performance bias, the ambiguous intervention definition or the apparent sample overlap, and they equate P<.05 with a positive effect.

signalling.question: A. Did the interpretation of findings address all of the concerns identified in the phase 2 assessment?
signalling.quote: we included a considerable number of studies with very small sample sizes, which may increase the risk of type I error and inflate the effect sizes [p14]; Our findings confirm the viability of multicomponent exercise as a management strategy for patients with dementia and MCI. [p1]

signalling.question: B. Was the relevance of identified studies to the review's research question appropriately considered?
signalling.quote: In addition, the measurement tools applied to identify diagnoses of dementia or MCI differed between studies

signalling.question: C. Did the reviewers avoid emphasising results on the basis of their statistical significance?
signalling.quote: P<.05 indicated that the intervention had a positive effect.

applicability.rationale: The eligibility criteria admitted exercise combined with non-exercise co-interventions (behavioural and cognitive therapy, electrical or magnetic stimulation), so the pooled 'exercise' effect may include co-intervention effects. The MCI pool may also include mixed dementia/MCI samples (Herrero; Mak).

overall_rationale: There are high concerns in domains 1 (ambiguous, internally contradictory intervention criterion; English only), 2 (narrow terms, no supplementary searching, language and format restrictions) and 4 (I2 = 93% unexplored, heterogeneous instruments pooled, apparent double counting of one MCI trial sample, primary-study bias not addressed). The phase 3 interpretation does not temper the conclusions accordingly.
